claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a fine, high-grain-boundary-density FCC microstructure.
Rapid solidification may leave minor compositional heterogeneity in the as-built alloy.
High grain-boundary density in the as-built alloy accelerates oxidation at grain boundaries.
High grain-boundary density accelerates reduction-induced destabilization at grain boundaries.
Localized grain-boundary degradation weakens intergranular cohesion and causes catastrophic failure.
Annealing at 950–1050 °C can coarsen the alloy's grains without inducing undesirable phase transformations.
Grain boundaries act as fast diffusion paths for oxygen or reducing species.
Fast transport along grain boundaries causes preferential oxidation or destabilization of Al and Ti at those boundaries.
Oxidizing exposure produces brittle, non-adherent Al2O3 and TiO2 layers along grain boundaries.
A reducing atmosphere destabilizes the protective oxide and exposes less resistant phases.
Oxidation and reduction-induced scale destabilization both accelerate intergranular degradation and ultimately cause catastrophic mechanical failure.
Grain coarsening reduces the total grain-boundary area.
Reducing grain-boundary area diminishes deleterious oxide or reduced-species formation along grain boundaries.
Grain coarsening will produce slower oxidation kinetics than the as-built fine-grained condition.
Grain-coarsened samples will form a more continuous and adherent protective scale than as-built samples.
Grain-coarsened samples will exhibit fewer cracks and delayed or prevented catastrophic failure relative to as-built samples.
The as-built fine-grained baseline will undergo rapid intergranular degradation and early catastrophic failure under the specified exposures.
Grain-size-dependent oxidation behavior is applicable near 900 °C for approximately 100 hours in air.
The proposed behavior remains relevant up to about 1000 °C in both oxidizing and reducing service atmospheres.
At significantly higher temperatures or under drastically different environments, other degradation mechanisms may dominate.
